visual_goal: Show the lifecycle of a breaking change to a canonical event: both versions published until consumers migrate and one quarter close ties out on both, v1 retired only at a month start outside year-end, and its schema kept readable for replay.
prompt: A board-game path of rounded stepping stones from left to right; each stone carries its own label written once, inside the stone, and each stone is joined to the next by one arrow. 'Proposed' with a small lightbulb, then 'Approved' with a stamp tick, then a wider stone 'Dual publish' on which two envelopes sit side by side, one tagged 'v1' and one tagged 'v2', with a small circular arrow above it where little consumer boxes move from the v1 envelope to the v2 envelope. Next 'Verified' with a closed ledger book and a green tick, and the words 'quarter close' written once, inside the 'Verified' stone just under the book. Next 'v1 deprecated' with the v1 envelope greyed. Next 'v1 retired' with a small flag planted on the first square of a blank grid, and the words 'month start' written once, inside the 'v1 retired' stone just under the grid. At the far right 'Readable' with an archive box holding the v1 envelope and a rewind arrow above it for replay.
alt: A path from Proposed and Approved to Dual publish, where v1 and v2 envelopes are both sent while consumers migrate, then Verified after a quarter close, v1 deprecated, v1 retired at a month start, and finally Readable in an archive for replay.

visual_goal: Show Northmere's target topology: producers publish canonical events through adapters onto Kafka; the hub validates, enriches with reference keys, counts and routes; each consumer gets its delivery shape and every vendor ledger sits behind its own anti-corruption layer; business rules live at the edges.
prompt: A left-to-right architecture illustration. At the far left, a vertical stack of six small plain storefront and service boxes grouped under one label 'Producers'; each has a small plug adapter on its right side, and one plug carries the label 'Adapter kit'. One arrow from each producer into a long vertical pipe with lightning bolts labeled 'Kafka'. One arrow from the pipe into a central rounded box labeled 'Hub' containing three small unlabeled icons in a row: a checkmark shield, a key, and a clipboard with tally marks. Above the hub, a box 'Schema registry' with one dashed arrow down into the hub; below the hub, a box 'Reference data' with one arrow up into the hub. A small bin labeled 'Quarantine' hangs below-right of the hub with one arrow into it. From the hub, five arrows fan out to the right to five consumer boxes stacked top to bottom: 'Subledger', 'FinDB', 'BlackLine', 'Workday', 'Fusion'; the boxes 'Workday' and 'Fusion' each have a small shield adapter on the arrow just before them. From 'Subledger' one arrow continues right through a small shield adapter into an open ledger book 'S/4HANA'. All arrows are plain lines without icons on them. Each producer box and each consumer box has one tiny gear inside its own box, showing that business rules live at the edges; the hub box and the pipe have no gears.
alt: Producers publish through adapter kits onto Kafka; a simple hub validates, adds reference keys, counts and routes, rejects to quarantine, and delivers to the subledger, FinDB, BlackLine, Workday and Fusion, with vendor ledgers including S/4HANA behind their own adapter layers.
